name: Teleférico de Lisboa (Lisbon Cable Car)
seoTitle: Lisbon Cable Car: Fares, Hours and When to Ride
tagline: A 10-minute gondola ride along the river in Parque das Nações, worth adding to an Oceanário visit rather than crossing the city for

description.short: A gondola lift built for Expo '98 that runs 1,230 m along the riverfront of Parque das Nações, between the Oceanário and the Vasco da Gama Tower, about 30 m above the water's edge. A one-way adult ticket costs €7.50.
description.full:
The cable car is a short ride, eight to twelve minutes each way, so on its own it does not justify the trip from the ship. It works as an add-on: if you are already going to the Oceanário or walking the Parque das Nações waterfront, it gives you a raised view of the district, the river and the Vasco da Gama Bridge for €7.50.

From the terminal, walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia and take a suburban train to Oriente, or take a taxi (about 15 minutes). The south station is on Passeio de Neptuno next to the Oceanário; the north station is on Passeio das Tágides beside the Vasco da Gama Tower, now a hotel.

The best use of time is one way only. Ride from the Oceanário end north, looking towards the bridge, then walk back along the river; the line follows the promenade, so the walk is easy and flat. A return ticket costs €9.50 and suits anyone who would rather not walk. Children aged 3 to 12 pay €5.50 one way and €6.50 return. There is no separate senior fare on the cable car itself, but the combined cable car and Oceanário ticket has one (€25.30 for over-65s, €33.90 for adults).

Opening hours change through the year: 11:00 to 19:00 until 23 October 2026, then 11:00 to 18:00 until 12 March 2027, with longer summer hours (10:30 to 20:00) from late May to mid-September. It does not run before 10:30 in any season, so it cannot be your first stop on an early arrival. Queues build on weekend afternoons; weekday mornings after opening are quietest.

Tickets must be bought before boarding. They are non-refundable but do not expire, which helps if wind or a schedule change stops you riding.
description.history: The gondola lift entered service in March 1998, two months before Expo '98 opened, and was one of the fair's most used attractions. It was built to carry visitors along the riverfront of the exhibition site, the former industrial land that became Parque das Nações. The equipment is by Doppelmayr: a detachable monocable system with 40 enclosed cabins for eight passengers, nine towers set in the riverbed and a 1,230 m line. It is run by the concession company Telecabine Lisboa, which carries out daily inspections and external audits every three years.
description.significance: It is one of the few pieces of Expo '98 infrastructure still doing what it was built for, and the only place in Lisbon where you see the eastern riverfront from above. For a cruise passenger it is a short, seated, low-effort way to take in the scale of Parque das Nações, the Tagus estuary and the bridge without walking the whole promenade.

directions.general: Located in Parque das Nações waterfront area, with stations at both northern end (near Oceanário) and southern end (near Vasco da Gama Tower)
directions.fromCruisePort: About 7.4 km north-east in Parque das Nações. Take the train from Santa Apolónia station (10 minutes' walk from the terminal) to Oriente, then walk 10 minutes to the southern cable car station near the Oceanarium. Taxi about 15 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro Red Line to Oriente station, then short walk to cable car stations. Trains to Oriente station from multiple Lisbon stations. Buses 705, 725, 728, 744, 708, 750, 759, 782, 794
directions.parking: Vasco da Gama Shopping Center underground parking, or Parque das Nações public car parks along waterfront

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily; hours vary by season and may change without notice
closedDates: Can close for several weeks of annual maintenance in late autumn (17 November to 5 December in 2025); check before visiting in November or December

admissionPrices.notes: One way: adults (13+) €7.50, children 3-12 €5.50. Return: adults €9.50, children €6.50. Under 3 free. No separate senior fare. Cable car return + Oceanário: adults (13-64) €33.90, seniors 65+ €25.30, children 3-12 €21.50. Tickets must be bought before boarding; no refunds, but tickets do not expire.

visitingInformation.averageVisitDuration: 8-12 minutes each way; 30-40 minutes including the walk back
visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Weekday mornings soon after opening, or late afternoon for lower sun over the river. It never opens before 10:30.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Buy a one-way ticket and walk back along the promenade. Combine with the Oceanário using the joint ticket. Tickets do not expire, so a wind closure does not waste them.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2-2.5 hours return for the cable car and a walk along the river; half a day with the Oceanário
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Train from Santa Apolónia to Oriente, then about 10-15 minutes on foot to the south station by the Oceanário, or a 15-minute taxi from the terminal.
tips: Buy a one-way ticket (€7.50) and walk back along the flat riverside promenade instead of paying €9.50 for a return.
Ride north from the Oceanário end to face the Vasco da Gama Bridge for most of the trip.
It never opens before 10:30 (11:00 for most of the year), so plan the Oceanário first if you arrive early.
Over-65s pay the full adult fare on the cable car; the combined ticket with the Oceanário has a senior rate (€25.30).
Children under 3 ride free; ages 3 to 12 pay €5.50 one way.
Tickets are non-refundable but never expire, so you can still use them if the line is stopped on your day.
Check the website before a November or December call: in 2025 the line closed from 17 November to 5 December for maintenance.
Online tickets are sold through the Oceanário's ticket site.

highlights: 1,230 m line along the riverfront, about 30 m above the ground
Views of the Vasco da Gama Bridge and the Tagus estuary
Overhead view of the Oceanário, the Portugal Pavilion and the arena
Enclosed cabins for up to eight passengers
Stations next to the Oceanário (south) and the Vasco da Gama Tower (north)
Combined ticket with the Oceanário available
facilities: Ticket offices at ground level in both stations
Boarding on the upper floor of each station
Online tickets through the Oceanário ticket site
Cafés and toilets nearby at the Oceanário and the shopping centre

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Ticket offices are at ground level and boarding takes place on the upper floor of each station. Cabins slow down in the stations for boarding. Wheelchair users should contact Telecabine Lisboa (+351 218 956 143) before visiting to confirm access.
